authorities.name: Equality Act 2010, s.20
authorities.date_note: Enactment year. The text verified this session is the current in-force version.
authorities.proposition: The duty to make reasonable adjustments comprises three requirements (s.20(2)); the first is that, where a provision, criterion or practice puts a disabled person at a substantial disadvantage compared with non-disabled persons, the duty-bearer must take such steps as it is reasonable to have to take to avoid the disadvantage (s.20(3)) - a deliberately open-textured 'reasonable steps' standard, not a fixed checklist.
authorities.verification_note: Fetched live and directly this session, on two independent passes, word-for-word consistent both times.

authorities.name: FirstGroup Plc v Paulley
authorities.judge_or_panel: Lord Neuberger (leading judgment), Lady Hale, Lord Kerr, Lord Clarke, Lord Sumption, Lord Reed, Lord Toulson
authorities.proposition: Fixes the s.20(3) reasonableness standard at a middle point for competing-service-user situations. A bus company's policy of instructing drivers simply to request a non-wheelchair user to vacate a wheelchair space, with no further action if the request is refused, fell short of the duty - once a refusal looks unreasonable, a driver should be expected to do more, such as rephrasing the request more firmly or considering a brief pause to encourage compliance. But an absolute rule mandating physical enforcement (compelling a passenger to move) would itself not be a reasonable step, given the practical risk of confrontation. The duty therefore requires meaningful further effort, short of coercive enforcement.
authorities.verification_note: Fetched live and directly from Find Case Law this session, independently re-fetched - both fetches confirmed paragraphs 66-67 discuss this middle-standard point, quoting different specific sentences within those paragraphs. The researching agent could not obtain a second independent full-text source (BAILII returned HTTP 403; the Supreme Court's own PDF failed twice with a socket error) and reported this limitation honestly rather than fabricating a workaround.

edges.verified_via: Paulley v FirstGroup [2017] UKSC 4, paras 46, 51, 66-67, fetched directly from Find Case Law and independently re-confirmed: construes s.20(3)'s 'reasonable steps' as requiring meaningful additional effort beyond a bare unenforced request, but stopping short of coercive/absolute enforcement.

what_this_is_not: Two verified nodes covering the reasonable-adjustments middle standard for competing-user situations. Does not cover the definition of disability under s.6, physical-feature or auxiliary-aid adjustments in detail, or any other Disability Law subject - all remain unbuilt.
